stories.text: On Saturday morning, Mrs. Adaeze Okafor opened her small bakery on Elm Street at six o'clock. Her son Chidi carried three trays of bread from the oven to the front window. A tall man in a green coat bought two loaves of rye and a lemon cake. Later, it began to rain, so Chidi brought the chalkboard sign inside. By noon, every loaf was gone, and Mrs. Okafor closed the shop early.
qs: How many trays did Chidi carry?
What did the man in the green coat buy?
two loaves of rye and a lemon cake
Why did Chidi bring the sign inside?

stories.text: Kenji Watanabe takes his dog, Biscuit, to Maple Park every evening after work. On Tuesday, Biscuit chased a red ball into the pond and came out covered in mud. Kenji had to wash him with a garden hose behind the apartment building. While he was drying the dog, his neighbor Mrs. Lindqvist offered him an old blue towel. Kenji thanked her and promised to bake her cookies on the weekend.
qs: What is the name of Kenji's dog?
Where does Kenji take the dog every evening?
What did Biscuit chase into the pond?
What did Kenji promise to bake?

stories.text: Dr. Meera Patel arrived at the Riverside Clinic at eight fifteen on Monday. Her first patient was a seven-year-old boy named Lucas who had a sore throat. She looked at his throat with a small flashlight and gave his mother a prescription for medicine. Because the waiting room was crowded, Dr. Patel skipped her lunch break. At five o'clock, she drove home and fell asleep on the sofa.
qs: When did Dr. Patel arrive at the clinic?
What did she use to look at his throat?
Why did Dr. Patel skip her lunch break?
because the waiting room was crowded

stories.text: Grandpa Tomas and his granddaughter Elena went fishing at Clearwater Lake before sunrise. They rowed a small wooden boat to the middle of the lake. Elena caught a silver trout, but Grandpa Tomas caught only an old boot. They laughed so loudly that a heron flew away from the reeds. On the way home, they stopped at a gas station and bought hot chocolate.
qs: What kind of boat did they row?
What did they buy at the gas station?

stories.text: Amira Haddad works at the city library on Fourth Avenue. Every Thursday afternoon, she reads stories aloud to children in the basement room. This week she chose a book about a lost penguin. Twelve children came, and one girl brought her own toy penguin to show everyone. After the reading, Amira gave each child a bookmark shaped like a fish.
qs: the city library on fourth avenue
When does she read stories to children?

stories.text: The Nguyen family moved into a yellow house on Cedar Lane in early August. Mr. Nguyen rented a truck, and his brother Bao helped him carry the heavy piano. The youngest daughter, Linh, chose the bedroom with the round window. That night they were too tired to cook, so they ordered pizza and ate it on the floor. The next morning, a neighbor named Mr. Brooks brought them a basket of tomatoes.
qs: What color is the Nguyen family's house?
Who helped Mr. Nguyen carry the piano?
the bedroom with the round window
they were too tired to cook

stories.text: Sofia Rossi missed the 7:40 train to Milan because her alarm clock did not ring. She waited forty minutes on the cold platform for the next one. While she waited, she bought a coffee and a newspaper from a small kiosk. On the train, she sat next to an old man who was knitting a scarf. She arrived at her office just in time for the meeting with Mr. Bianchi.
qs: because her alarm clock did not ring
her alarm clock did not ring
How long did she wait on the platform?
What was the old man knitting?

stories.text: In April, Mr. Hamid Rahimi planted carrots, beans and sunflowers in his backyard garden. He watered them every morning with a green watering can. In June, rabbits ate most of the beans, so he built a low fence of wire. By September, the sunflowers were taller than his garage. He gave the seeds to his granddaughter, Parisa, who fed them to the birds.
qs: When did Mr. Rahimi plant his garden?
What ate most of the beans?
Who fed the seeds to the birds?

stories.text: Jamal turned ten on a snowy Friday in January. His aunt Keisha baked a chocolate cake with ten blue candles. His best friend, Owen, gave him a book about dinosaurs. During the party, the lights went out for a few minutes because of the storm. Everyone sang in the dark, and Jamal said it was the best birthday he ever had.
qs: Why did the lights go out?
on a snowy friday in january

stories.text: Mrs. Ingrid Larsen has a gray cat named Pepper who likes to sleep in the laundry basket. One afternoon, Pepper disappeared, and Mrs. Larsen searched the whole house. She looked under the beds, behind the curtains and inside the closet. Finally, she heard a soft meow coming from the dryer. Pepper had climbed in with the warm towels and fallen asleep.
qs: Where does Pepper like to sleep?
Where was the meow coming from?
What had Pepper climbed in with?

stories.text: Every Sunday, Carlos Mendoza sells fruit at the farmers' market near the old church. He arrives at five in the morning to set up his striped tent. His most popular fruit is the mango, which he brings from his cousin's farm. Last Sunday, a woman bought twenty mangoes for her daughter's wedding. Carlos gave her a free pineapple as a gift.
qs: at the farmers' market near the old church
Where does the mango come from?
How many mangoes did the woman buy?
Why did the woman buy the mangoes?

stories.text: The children of Hillside School performed a play about a brave mouse on Wednesday evening. Priya played the mouse, and her classmate Daniel played the hungry cat. Their teacher, Ms. Alvarez, painted the background of a forest on large sheets of cardboard. In the middle of the play, Daniel's whiskers fell off, and the audience laughed. At the end, the parents clapped for a long time.
qs: What did she paint the background on?

stories.text: On a hot afternoon, Femi noticed that the back tire of his bicycle was flat. He pushed the bike to Mr. Adeyemi's repair shop at the end of Palm Road. Mr. Adeyemi found a small nail stuck in the rubber. He fixed the tire in fifteen minutes and charged Femi only two dollars. Femi rode home quickly to show his sister, Bisi.
qs: What was wrong with Femi's bicycle?
the back tire of his bicycle was flat
at the end of palm road
What was stuck in the rubber?
How much did Mr. Adeyemi charge?

stories.text: Last summer, Hannah and her father climbed Mount Briar, a steep hill north of their town. They started at seven o'clock and carried sandwiches, apples and two bottles of water. Halfway up, Hannah twisted her ankle on a loose rock. Her father wrapped it with a scarf, and they rested under a pine tree. They reached the top at noon and saw three lakes below them.
qs: hannah twisted her ankle on a loose rock
How many lakes did they see?

stories.text: Mr. and Mrs. Kowalski celebrated their anniversary at a small Italian restaurant called Luna. The waiter, a young man named Marco, brought them a candle and two glasses of water. Mr. Kowalski ordered spaghetti, and his wife chose the mushroom soup. When the bill came, Mr. Kowalski realized he had left his wallet at home. Luckily, Mrs. Kowalski paid with her own card and teased him all the way home.
qs: Where had Mr. Kowalski left his wallet?

stories.text: Aiko could not find her house key when she came home from school on Thursday. She checked her backpack twice and then sat on the front steps. Her neighbor, Mr. Sato, saw her and invited her to wait in his kitchen. He made her a cup of green tea while they waited for her mother. Later, her mother found the key in the pocket of Aiko's raincoat.
qs: When could Aiko not find her key?
when she came home from school on thursday
What did Mr. Sato make her?
in the pocket of aiko's raincoat

stories.text: On the first day of July, the Silva family drove four hours to the beach at Porto Azul. Lucas built a sandcastle with a deep moat, and his sister Ana collected shells. Their mother read a novel under a big orange umbrella. In the afternoon, a wave knocked down the castle, and Lucas was upset. Ana gave him her prettiest shell to cheer him up.
qs: How long did the family drive?
Why did Ana give Lucas her prettiest shell?

stories.text: Mr. Diego Fuentes is a carpenter who lives in a village near the mountains. Last month, the village school asked him to build six new benches for the playground. He used oak wood because it is strong and lasts a long time. His apprentice, a quiet girl named Rosa, sanded each bench until it was smooth. The children painted their names on the benches with bright colors.
qs: How many benches did he build?
Why did he use oak wood?
because it is strong and lasts a long time
it is strong and lasts a long time
his apprentice, a quiet girl named rosa
What did the children paint on the benches?

stories.text: It was raining hard when Olivia waited for the number 12 bus outside the post office. Her umbrella broke in the wind, so she held a newspaper over her head. The bus came ten minutes late, and the driver apologized to everyone. Olivia sat by the window and watched people running through the puddles. When she got off at Station Square, the rain had stopped.
qs: Which bus did Olivia wait for?
What did she hold over her head?

stories.text: Ravi spent his school holiday on his uncle's farm in Punjab. His uncle owned a brown horse named Sultan and a field full of wheat. Every morning, Ravi gave Sultan two carrots and brushed his mane. One evening, Sultan broke the gate and ran into the neighbor's field. Ravi and his uncle found him an hour later, eating grass beside a well.
qs: Where did Ravi spend his holiday?
on his uncle's farm in punjab
How many carrots did Ravi give Sultan?
What was Sultan doing when they found him?

stories.text: Mei Chen practiced the violin for three months before her first concert. The concert took place in the town hall on a Saturday in May. Her grandmother came all the way from Shanghai to listen. Mei was nervous, and her hands shook while she tuned the strings. However, she played without a single mistake, and her grandmother cried with joy.
qs: Where did the concert take place?
Where did her grandmother come from?

stories.text: During the night, half a meter of snow fell on the small town of Kirkby. In the morning, Mr. Ellis cleared his driveway with a wide shovel. His twin sons, Ben and Sam, built a snowman with a carrot nose and a striped hat. The schools were closed, so the boys spent the whole day sledding on Hawthorn Hill. In the evening, their mother made a pot of beef stew.
qs: What did Mr. Ellis use to clear his driveway?
What are the names of the twin sons?
Where did the boys go sledding?

stories.text: Mrs. Fatima Benali works as a pharmacist in a shop on Harbor Street. On Friday, an elderly man named Mr. Duval came in with a bad cough. She sold him a bottle of cough syrup and told him to drink plenty of warm water. Mr. Duval forgot his glasses on the counter. Mrs. Benali ran after him and returned them before he reached the corner.

Paolo's parrot, Kiwi, can say ten words in Spanish and three in English. Every morning, Kiwi shouts 'Good morning' when Paolo opens the kitchen curtains. Last week, Kiwi learned to copy the sound of the doorbell. Paolo ran to the door five times before he understood the joke. Now he keeps the bird's cage in the living room, far from the front door.
qs: How many words can Kiwi say in Spanish?
What did Kiwi learn last week?
to copy the sound of the doorbell
How many times did Paolo run to the door?
Where does Paolo keep the cage now?

stories.text: After finishing university, Grace Mwangi got her first job at a bookshop in Nairobi. Her boss, Mr. Otieno, taught her how to use the cash register. On her first day, she sold forty-two books and helped a lost tourist find a map. At closing time, she was so tired that she forgot her scarf in the storeroom. The next morning, Mr. Otieno had folded it neatly on her desk.
qs: Where did Grace get her first job?
How many books did she sell on her first day?
What did the lost tourist need?
Where did she forget her scarf?

stories.text: The Green Hawks played their final football match of the season against the Riverside Lions on Sunday. The score was tied at one goal each until the last minute. Then their captain, Mateo, kicked the ball from far away, and it flew into the net. The players lifted their coach, Mr. Garcia, onto their shoulders. That night, they celebrated with pizza at Tony's Diner.
qs: Who did the Green Hawks play against?

stories.text: On Wednesday night, a pipe burst under Mrs. Yilmaz's kitchen sink. Water covered the floor, and her slippers floated toward the door. She called a plumber named Mr. Hughes, who arrived forty minutes later. He replaced the broken pipe with a new copper one. Mrs. Yilmaz offered him a slice of baklava, and he ate two.
qs: What did he replace the pipe with?
How many slices of baklava did he eat?

stories.text: Late one night, Noor heard a strange hooting outside her bedroom window. She turned on her flashlight and saw a small brown owl sitting on the fence. The owl had a hurt wing and could not fly. In the morning, Noor and her mother drove it to the animal hospital in Westbrook. A vet named Dr. Kim promised to call them when the owl was healthy again.
qs: Why could the owl not fly?
the owl had a hurt wing
Where did they take the owl?
to the animal hospital in westbrook

stories.text: Mr. Aurelio Santos paints pictures of boats in a small studio above a fish shop. Every morning he opens the window to hear the seagulls. His favorite painting shows a red fishing boat at sunset. A rich visitor from Lisbon offered to buy it for a thousand euros. Mr. Santos refused because the boat once belonged to his father.
qs: What does his favorite painting show?
a red fishing boat at sunset
How much did the visitor offer?
because the boat once belonged to his father
the boat once belonged to his father

stories.text: Zainab woke up on Monday with a fever and a headache. Her father called her school and said she would stay home. He made her rice soup and brought her an extra blanket. In the afternoon, her friend Chloe dropped off the homework and a funny card. By Wednesday, Zainab felt well enough to go back to class.
qs: When did Zainab wake up sick?
What did her father make her?
the homework and a funny card
When did Zainab go back to class?

stories.text: Mr. Jonas Weber flew from Berlin to Toronto for his sister's wedding. At the airport, his suitcase did not come out on the belt. A woman at the help desk wrote down his address and promised to send the bag to his hotel. That evening, Jonas bought a shirt and a tie in a shop near the hotel. The suitcase arrived the next morning, two hours before the ceremony.
qs: Where did Mr. Weber fly to?
What did not come out on the belt?
the next morning, two hours before the ceremony

stories.text: On the hottest day of August, Leo and his little brother Max walked to the ice cream shop on Bay Road. Leo ordered strawberry, and Max chose chocolate with sprinkles. Max's scoop fell onto the pavement before he could taste it. The shop owner, Mrs. Petrova, saw what happened and gave him a new one for free. The boys thanked her and ate their ice cream on a bench by the harbor.
qs: Where is the ice cream shop?
max's scoop fell onto the pavement
Who gave Max a new one?
Where did the boys eat their ice cream?
on a bench by the harbor

stories.text: Old Mr. MacLeod has kept sheep on the island of Skerra for forty years. Every spring, he and his dog, Rory, bring the flock down from the hills. This year, a lamb got stuck between two rocks near the cliff. Rory barked until Mr. MacLeod came and lifted the lamb free. That night, Mr. MacLeod gave Rory an extra piece of meat.
qs: Where does Mr. MacLeod keep sheep?
How long has he kept sheep?
Where did the lamb get stuck?
between two rocks near the cliff
What did Mr. MacLeod give Rory?

stories.text: Every Tuesday evening, Mrs. Esperanza Ruiz takes a computer class at the community center. She is seventy-one years old and wants to send emails to her grandchildren in Canada. Her teacher, a patient young man named Arjun, showed her how to attach a photo. On her first try, she sent a picture of her kitchen floor by mistake. Her grandchildren replied with lots of laughing faces.
qs: Where does Mrs. Ruiz take a computer class?
Why does she take the class?
wants to send emails to her grandchildren in canada
to send emails to her grandchildren
a patient young man named arjun
What did she send by mistake?
a picture of her kitchen floor

stories.text: Tobias found an old pocket watch in a wooden box in his grandmother's attic. The watch had stopped at a quarter past three. He took it to a watchmaker named Mr. Feld, whose shop was on Lindenstrasse. Mr. Feld cleaned the gears and replaced a tiny spring. When Tobias wound the watch, it began to tick again for the first time in fifty years.
qs: in a wooden box in his grandmother's attic
At what time had the watch stopped?

stories.text: Ji-woo invited her friends Isabel and Kofi to cook dinner at her flat on Saturday. They made dumplings filled with cabbage and pork. Kofi was in charge of the dough, but he added too much water. Isabel fixed it by adding more flour. They ate forty dumplings together and watched an old movie until midnight.
qs: Whose flat did they cook at?
What were the dumplings filled with?
Who was in charge of the dough?
How did Isabel fix the dough?
How many dumplings did they eat?

stories.text: Mr. Oskar Nilsen was the keeper of the lighthouse at Gull Point. Each evening at sunset, he climbed one hundred and twelve steps to light the lamp. One stormy night, he saw a small sailboat drifting near the rocks. He called the coast guard on his radio, and a rescue boat arrived within twenty minutes. The two sailors on the boat later sent him a letter of thanks.
qs: How many steps did he climb?
What did he see near the rocks?
Who did he call on his radio?
What did the sailors send him?

stories.text: Mr. Kwame Asante is a tailor with a shop next to the train station. Two days before his daughter's graduation, he began sewing her a dress from green silk. He worked late every night under a single lamp. On the morning of the graduation, he sewed the last button just as the taxi arrived. His daughter, Ama, said it was the most beautiful dress in the hall.
qs: What was the dress made from?
When did he sew the last button?
on the morning of the graduation

stories.text: On a school trip, Mr. Haruto Ito's class visited the natural history museum in the capital. The students saw a whale skeleton hanging from the ceiling of the main hall. A boy named Felix wandered off to look at the meteorites and got lost. A guard found him twenty minutes later near the gift shop. Mr. Ito made Felix hold his hand for the rest of the visit.
qs: What was hanging from the ceiling?

stories.text: Every Saturday at nine, Isla takes swimming lessons at the public pool on Grove Street. Her coach, Mrs. Abebe, used to swim for her country. For weeks, Isla was afraid to put her face in the water. Last Saturday, she finally swam the whole length of the pool without stopping. Mrs. Abebe gave her a small gold sticker shaped like a star.
qs: When does Isla take swimming lessons?
What was Isla afraid to do?
to put her face in the water
put her face in the water
What did Mrs. Abebe give her?
a small gold sticker shaped like a star
